sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real decision, by when, and which numbers frame it?
criteria: Restates the decision as the smallest org change that passes the review at month 9 without touching the restoration commitment or the rate case
Derives the governance workload (103 person-weeks) and the review window (39 weeks)
Names the three hard floors: headcount frozen at 40, data science at 13 or more, grid operations squad untouched
States at least one thing out of scope

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers at least the CEO or board, the CRO, the VP of Rates and the SVP of Electric Operations, each with a distinct want
Says what the VP of Rates gives up (3 data scientists, leaving the team at its floor of 13) and what they get in return
Includes the 40 staff, and treats the 3 people who move as a separate group
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real org options, and how does each fare on the review, the restoration commitment and people?
criteria: Includes 'change nothing' (or a steering committee only) as an option
Counts how many of the 40 change manager under each option
Shows that 3 in-house validators cannot finish 103 person-weeks alone (93 available), so outside validation is needed
Compares options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What org do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would make you change it?
criteria: Makes one clear recommendation with governance reporting outside the AI and business lines
Names what is given up, including direct control of the squads and data science left at its floor
Says which moves are hard to reverse and why the recommendation keeps later options open
Gives a dated revisit (month 12) with measurable triggers

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does each option cost or save over three years, in cash and in people?
criteria: Prices vendor consolidation over the same 3-year horizon for every option ($0.6M a year from month 6)
Prices reorg attrition from the number of people changing manager, with the assumption labelled
Prices the restoration risk as an expected slip in the $12M ramp, not as zero
Separates cash from freed capacity of people already on payroll

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who reports to whom, and who decides what?
criteria: Gives the new structure with headcounts that add up to 40
Puts validators under the CRO, not under the VP of AI or a business head
Says how standards bind teams that don't report to you (the contract, the gateway, the inventory)
Names one owner for the review readiness

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens between the board meeting and month 12?
criteria: Moves the 3 validators by about week 8 and finishes validation before the review
Times the contract consolidation to the renewals within 6 months
Has at least one gate with a measurable threshold
Includes the month-12 revisit as a milestone

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong, including the HR and legal process of the reorg itself?
criteria: Picks the 3 people who move by stated criteria, asks for volunteers first, and keeps level and pay unchanged
Covers the risk that data science at 13 loses one more person, with a named response
Covers squads bypassing the shared gateway or contract
Has HR and legal review the role changes before anyone is told

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the org works, and what would show it is causing harm?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks attrition in the groups that changed manager against the 15% baseline
Tracks the restoration run-rate against the $12M commitment
Measures validation so it can't quietly become a release bottleneck

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and in what order?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least five audiences
Tells the people who change manager before the wider announcement, in person
Tells the board the cost of the design and what is deliberately left for month 12
Sets a cadence and an order of announcement
